Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 02.03.2020 passed by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Shivamogga (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.986/2017.

II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Shivamogga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under; That on 05.03.2017 at about 11.20 p.m., Malthesh was driving the lorry bearing registration No.KA-14-B- 2492 belonging to one Venkatesh H.R., the said lorry was driven from Siddapura with load of akeshiya and while proceeding on Sirsi-Siddapura road near Kanagodu, respondent No.2, who was the driver of the offending NC: 2024:KHC:2161 vehicle bearing registration No.MP-33-H-3350 drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety and suddenly took right turn without any indication and without following the rules and regulations dashed against the right side of lorry driven by Malthesh, due to which the accident occurred, respondent No.2 without stopping the vehicle fled away from the spot.
However, the vehicle of respondent No.2 was stopped by the help of local people and he was apprehended.
Due to the impact of the accident, the said Malthesh succumbed to the injuries.
3.1 It is stated that the deceased was aged 29 years, he was survived by the claimants, who are the legal representatives and he was the sole bread winner of the family.
The claimants were dependent on him financially, emotionally and they have lost the love and affection of the deceased, due to the death having occurred in the road traffic accident.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 remained absent and they were placed ex parte.

Respondent No.3-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections and took up the plea that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself, he was not possessing valid and effective driving licence and the lorry did not possess valid transport permit and fitness certificate and also denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation and income.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and another witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P22.

On the other hand, NC: 2024:KHC:2161 respondents did not adduce any evidence, but produced two documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.17,84,000/- with Jyothi M vs Vikram Singh Kansan on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89920619/
3 interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of order till the date of deposit and also held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 to be jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.3 being the insurer was directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of the order.
3.6

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the tribunal has committed an error in not awarding suitable compensation NC: 2024:KHC:2161 and has not taken into consideration the evidence adduced by the claimants with regard to income.
It is further contended that the tribunal has failed to award reasonable compensation under other heads.

Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation and to allow the appeal preferred by the claimants.
5.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference as the claimants have not produced any material evidence to show the proof of income, the tribunal has taken the income to be Rs.8,000/- as notional income, which does not call for interference.
It is further contended that the tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation under other heads, which does not call for interference.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the impugned judgment and award, it is not NC: 2024:KHC:2161 in dispute that the accident occurred on 05.03.2017 between two vehicles i.e., lorry driven by the deceased and the offending lorry which came in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the lorry of the deceased, due to which deceased fell down and died on the spot.
7. Now coming to the age, avocation and income as on the date of occurrence of accident, the tribunal assessed the income at Rs.8,000/-, which is on the lower side.

It applied the multiplier as '17', as the deceased was aged 29 years as on the date of occurrence of accident, so also, added 40%
towards future prospects and deducted 1/4th towards personal and living expenses, as there are five dependents, which do not call for interference and the same are retained.
The Legal Services Authority chart stipulates the notional income of Rs.11,000/- for the accident of the year 2017 as against Rs.8,000/- taken by the tribunal.

Therefore, the claimants would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.23,56,200/- (Rs.11,000/- + 40% = Rs.15,400/- - 1/4th = Rs.11,550/- x 12 x 17)
NC: 2024:KHC:2161 towards loss of dependency as against Rs.17,13,600/- awarded by the tribunal.
8. Towards loss of consortium, the tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/-.

I am in agreement with the learned counsel for appellants that as there are five dependents, each would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680.

10% escalation for one block period on the same to be awarded under this head, which would come to Rs.33,000/- (Rs.30,000/- + 10%).
